# Radoslav Radev Requires A Minimum 10-Second Hold Before Progressing To The Next Planche Or Front Lever Step

Radoslav Radev requires a minimum 10-second hold with good form on a planche or front lever progression before moving to the next harder step. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:46]

## Details

- For planche: before going from tuck planche to advanced planche, make sure you have minimum 10 seconds with good form and good technique. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:46]
- If you have 10 seconds you are ready, but not if you have two seconds. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:56]
- For front lever: before going from straddle front lever to full front lever, make sure you have at least 10 seconds clean straddle front lever. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 02:06]
- He also says not to wait too much: when you have 10 seconds, you are ready to move on. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:56]

## Evidence

- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:46 (Radoslav Radev): "let's say you are on tuck planche before you go to advanced planche make sure that you have minimum 10 seconds with good form good technique and then you're ready to go to advance"
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:56 (Radoslav Radev): "if you have 10 seconds you're ready but not if you have two seconds"
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:56 (Radoslav Radev): "also like the first advice that i gave you don't wait too much because you will waste also a lot of time so if you have 10 seconds you're ready"
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 02:06 (Radoslav Radev): "if you want to go from straddle front lever to full front lever, make sure that you have at least 10 seconds clean straddle front lever, and then you can go to the mini straddle or directly to the full."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:29 (Radoslav Radev): "Second, you're rushing the progressions. You try to go too fast. You skip levels and you don't control the basics. Every single skill has steps for a reason. If you can't control the easier progression, you have no business going the harder one this is also how the people get hurt"

## Why This Matters

He says that skipping levels and going to harder progressions without controlling the easier one is how people get hurt. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 01:29]
